solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Launder duvet? No time. Shaking esteemed too lightly

indicators.note: shaking things up jumbles them, so the remaining letters are rearranged
No here tells us to go without the letter for time

explanation.surface: A housework question about laundering a duvet, with no time to spare, wanders off into how someone was underrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' drops the T at the end of DUVET, and 'Shaking' rearranges LAUNDER plus DUVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to undervalue something is to rate it too low, which is to esteem it too lightly.

clue.text: Other than old women one who fails to appear for food

indicators.note: other than means excluding, so the letters for old women are taken away

parts.note: a no-show is someone who does not turn up
O for old and W for women together give OW

explanation.surface: Apart from the old women, someone who never turned up for the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O and W from NO-SHOW leaves the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: nosh is informal British English for grub or a meal.

clue.text: Old Irish Queen's to die at last

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen; with the possessive it gives ERS

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of die

explanation.surface: A historical line about an Irish queen dying at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen; her 's adds S, and 'at last' takes the final E of 'die'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland (and Scotland), so it fits Old Irish.

clue.text: Gullible one not in control in judicial decision

indicators.note: one not in control means the word for one stands where the letters for in control were

parts.note: a verdict is the decision reached in court
i/c, written IC, is the abbreviation for in charge, i.e. in control
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A naive person, not in charge, swept up in a court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one not in control' reads as 'one in place of in control'; the final 'in' is just a link placing it within the decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdant means green, and green is a common figurative sense of inexperienced or gullible.

clue.text: Act on new fabric

parts.note: an Act of Parliament is a law

explanation.surface: An instruction to take action on some new cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a fine, sheer linen or cotton cloth, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Imprison a hundred for beginning to subvert Lesotho for example

indicators.note: a hundred for the first of subvert means C replaces that letter

parts.note: to enslave is to hold someone captive, loosely to imprison them

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of subvert

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A political plot to lock people up and undermine the African kingdom of Lesotho.
explanation.walkthrough: C replaces the S of ENSLAVE. Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an enclave is a territory wholly surrounded by another state, which Lesotho is.

clue.text: Jan I dare say is upset after strange end to party

indicators.note: after places the rearranged words behind NEW and the final letter of party

parts.note: new can mean unfamiliar or strange

indicators.note: end to picks the final letter of party
upset means overturned, so dare and say are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone called Jan admits being upset after a party ended strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jan I' is read as January the first, not a person speaking. DARESAY is rearranged to EARSDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalence: January 1 is the first day of the calendar year, the holiday of that name.

clue.text: Pigment one's taken from Phyllis after mould is removed from a number

indicators.note: after puts the shortened Phyllis behind the shortened anaesthetic
is removed from tells us to take the word for mould out of the anaesthetic

parts.note: a number here is something that numbs, an anaesthetic such as chloroform
form can mean a mould or shape

indicators.note: taken from tells us to cut the letters for one's out of Phyllis

parts.note: one is I and the 's is is, so one's gives IS

explanation.surface: A scientific puzzle about a pigment, a woman named Phyllis, and mould being cleared off something numbered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a thing that numbs, not a figure. CHLOROFORM minus FORM gives CHLORO; PHYLLIS minus IS gives PHYLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plants that captures light for photosynthesis.

clue.text: Fourth man could make 19

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of another entry can be rearranged into this one

parts.note: 19 refers to the answer at 19 across, the short form of the book of Esther

explanation.surface: A puzzle-internal note that a certain fourth man could be built from another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ESTH (19 across) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical: after Adam, Cain and Abel, Seth was the next man in Genesis, making him the fourth.

clue.text: Russian heir cheers waits playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the words are frolicking about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian prince cheers the waits, the street carol singers, as they perform.
explanation.walkthrough: Waits are bands of carol singers who go door to door at Christmas, a British custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical title: the Tsesarevich was the heir apparent to the Russian throne.

clue.text: Novice Conservative going the wrong way head first

indicators.note: head first says the original leading letter is brought back to the front
going the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A beginner Tory politician rushing the wrong way, diving headlong.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY turned round is YROT; moving its T, which was the head of the word, back to the front gives the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tyro is a beginner or learner in some field.

clue.text: Attractive young woman sailing close to the wind after garment's removed although not hot

indicators.note: after puts the sailing term behind the rest
although not hot tells us to drop the letter for hot

parts.note: a habit is a garment, as worn by a monk or nun; the 's is read as is
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
off means taken away or removed
to luff is to sail nearer the wind

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a young woman taking a risk, garment off, even though the weather isn't hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'garment's' is read as 'is'; 'although not' is the instruction to drop the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang: a bit of fluff is a pretty young woman, now often seen as condescending.

clue.text: To write about wife, bridge player for a small amount

indicators.note: about means around, so the letter for wife goes inside to

parts.note: taken as written
to pen is to write
North is one of the four players in bridge

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a little about a wife and a bridge partner.
explanation.walkthrough: W sits inside TO to make TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: two pennies' worth means a trifling amount, as in giving your two pennyworth.

clue.text: Tom perhaps applying weapon to fish

parts.note: a bow is a weapon for shooting arrows
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone called Tom using a weapon on a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Bowling is the sailor of a well-known old English sea song, so Tom is an example of someone with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Tom Bowling is the title character of a famous Dibdin sea song.

clue.text: Narcotic nark

definitions.meaning: a police informer, or to inform on someone

explanation.surface: A drug-world informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two slang senses: one for cannabis, the other for someone who tells tales to the police.

clue.text: Liberal leaving a talkative party for wash seen in old bathroom

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for Liberal goes out of the phrase

parts.note: vocal means outspoken or talkative
do is informal for a party

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician walks out of a chatty gathering to have a wash in an old bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wash' is a thin coat of colour, not a bath: avocado green was a popular bathroom-suite colour in 1970s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: avocado was the classic dull-green shade of bathroom fittings decades ago.

clue.text: Sailor fired around

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
out means dismissed or fired

explanation.surface: A sailor discharged and wandering about.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: about and around both mean roughly or in the vicinity.

clue.text: Do out of payment for race

indicators.note: out of means the note's letters are taken from inside the payment

parts.note: a tribute is a payment made by one state to another
ut is the old name for do, the first note of the scale

explanation.surface: Someone cheated of their pay for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do out of' looks like cheat; in fact UT, the medieval name for the note do, comes out of TRIBUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a race in the older sense of a people or ethnic group is a tribe.

clue.text: Thanks to father for snack

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
pa is informal for father

explanation.surface: Saying thank you to Dad for a bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tapa is a small Spanish appetiser, a snack served with drinks.

clue.text: Short book is French; that's hard

parts.note: est is French for is
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A short book that is French, which is said to be tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: Esth is the short written form for the Old Testament book of Esther.

clue.text: Chief of police, we hear, took action against sham

indicators.note: chief of points to the leading letter of police
we hear tells us the following letters only sound like the phrase

parts.note: sued means took legal action against

explanation.surface: A police chief, so rumour says, took action against a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The P is silent in the answer, so the whole word is pronounced like 'sued'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a pseud is a pretentious person, a poser or fake intellectual.

clue.text: Less interesting supporters? That is right

parts.note: pros are people in favour, supporters

explanation.surface: Wondering whether supporters are duller, then agreeing that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative: prosy means dull and prosaic, so prosier is duller.

clue.text: It's most stupid to cook tart for holy man

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
a tart is a kind of pie
St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A remark that baking a tart for a saint is very foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of dopey, meaning dim-witted or stupid.

clue.text: Hand at French department may show them. So do other hands

definitions.text: Hand at French department may show them. So do other hands

parts.note: fin is slang for a hand
Gers is a department in south-west France

explanation.surface: A hand waving at a French region shows its digits, as other hands do.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: any hand displays these.
explanation.definitionFit: Every hand has digits, so the whole sentence describes what a hand shows.

clue.text: Work around return of snake to sheet

indicators.note: around says the work word wraps the snake

parts.note: to toil is to work hard

indicators.note: return of says the snake's word is read backwards

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Working around a snake that came back onto the bed sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheet' looks like bed linen, but it means a sail here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical: sheet is a poetic term for a sail, and a topsail is one.

clue.text: Sign is a third of a mile further

parts.note: the li is a Chinese unit of distance about a third of a mile long
on means further, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A sign saying a third of a mile further on.
explanation.definitionFit: Zodiac: Leo is the sign of this animal.

clue.text: Fruit for catching birds

definitions.meaning: birdlime, a sticky substance smeared on twigs to trap birds

explanation.surface: Fruit used as bait for catching birds.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for a sour citrus fruit and for the sticky paste spread to snare birds.

clue.text: One right for tree

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: One right answer for a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Genus: Acer is the maple family of trees.

clue.text: Get advanced nothing for shrub producing wrong colour here

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Getting nowhere with a plant whose dye comes out the wrong colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong colour here' refers to the puzzle's green theme: this shrub gives blue indigo dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany: anil is the West Indian indigo plant, a shrub yielding blue dye, not green.

clue.text: Old monarch in going down becomes greenish

parts.note: VRI, Victoria Regina et Imperatrix, is the old monarch, and in gives I, put inside it
a descent is a going down

explanation.surface: An old king in decline turns green.
explanation.walkthrough: VRI is Queen Victoria's royal cipher; I, for 'in', goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin-derived adjective: viridescent means becoming or slightly green.

clue.text: Holiday charge includes tea, we are told

indicators.note: includes means the charge holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: we are told signals a word that sounds like tea

parts.note: tea is pronounced like the letter T

explanation.surface: The holiday charge covers tea, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic sense: a fete is a festival or holiday, as well as a fundraising fair.

clue.text: New kind of dove? It makes good soup

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
the turtle dove is a kind of dove

explanation.surface: A novel breed of dove that is good for the soup pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this sea creature was the classic source of turtle soup.
